title: Understanding Automated Program Repair Agents through the Lens of Traceability: An Empirical Study
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
datasets: SWE-bench Verified, 500 Python issue tasks across 12 repositories; primary trace collection is 500 task instances. Also uses Verified-50 random subset for manual analysis and new reproducer generation/localization experiments.

Public Hugging Face dataset `zt6c3mxv8q/logs_and_trajs`: 3.28 GB trajectory/log repository documented to include agent predictions, metadata, trajectories, logs and results. Models/agent combinations include Agentless, AutoCodeRover, MASAI, SWE-Agent and OpenHands with Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4o (some combinations unavailable).
SWT-Bench/SWT-Bench-Lite appears in related work only; not used as the experimental benchmark.
models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o; test-generation/localization RQ uses Claude Sonnet 4.
license: Paper CC BY 4.0; software/trajectory license not specified
input_setting: Issue report + buggy repository snapshot from SWE-bench Verified; agents generate patches and sometimes reproducer/regression tests. Reproducer study varies Claude Sonnet 4 sampling count/temperature and Agentless localization context on Verified-50. Outputs are agent trajectories and tests; no root-cause taxonomy or per-bug causal label is produced.
reproduction_grade: B- (cached-trace analysis conditional/feasible; original full rerun needs commercial APIs and agent environments)
concept_hook: High for issue-reproduction fidelity, test overfitting and localization-informed test generation; no causal root-cause labels.
limitation: SWE-bench Verified is used experimentally; SWT-Bench is related work only. API/data license limits.
